critique.good: Fits the 360px box with all five columns visible, and keeps the plan columns in one horizontal band.
critique.problems: Unreadable: headers break into 'Enterpri se' and 'Not es', there are 26 mid-word splits, Notes becomes a 1–3 character ribbon, and rows balloon to 292–362px, making the table 1404px tall. Horizontal comparison is destroyed.
critique.cause: Every width is below its content minimum: Feature 82 (61px content), Free 78 (57px vs 79px for Community), Pro 64 (43px vs 66px for Unlimited), Enterprise 80 (59px vs 75px header), Notes 55 (34px vs 419px). Squeezing Notes to 55px forces character-level breaking and enormous row heights.

critique.good: No header wraps, no mid-word splits, compact 36/83px rows, and all plan values stay intact. This is the most scannable of the three.
critique.problems: Overflows by 211px; Notes is completely offscreen at 360px, and the first four columns sum to 390px, so even Enterprise is clipped in the initial view. Feature 90px makes 'SSO / SAML' wrap at the slash.
critique.cause: Widths were chosen for readable content, producing a 570px table. The allocation also over-spends on Pro (90px) and Enterprise (110px) while under-spending on Feature (90px).

critique.good: No header wraps; Notes at 240px is much more readable than in r0A or r0B, and most rows stay at 60px.
critique.problems: Still overflows by 241px and Notes is offscreen; two mid-word splits appear: 'Unlimite d' in Pro and 'Communit y' in Free. The Support row grows to 106px.
critique.cause: Free 92px gives 71px content for Community (needs 79px) and Pro 82px gives 61px for Unlimited (needs 66px), while Notes is given 240px. Width is redistributed away from the plan values that must stay intact.

critique.good: Feature, Free and Pro are wide enough for their labels and short values to stay on one line, with no mid-word splits. The top rows read cleanly and the plan values are easy to compare where visible.
critique.problems: Enterprise is clipped at the 360px box edge, so the three plans cannot be compared at a glance. The Support row grows to four lines in Enterprise, and the table overflows by 210px with Notes completely off-screen.
critique.cause: Enterprise is only 98px (77px text), too narrow for '24/7 phone & dedicated manager'. Notes at 180px still leaves just 159px for 419px of prose, so it wraps to three lines and inflates rows. Free at 100px and Pro at 87px are already at their no-split minima, so the width is being spent on Feature and Notes rather than the clipped Enterprise column.

critique.good: The most compact render: row heights are 60–83px, the tallest cell is three lines, and there are no mid-word splits. Plan values stay intact.
critique.problems: Notes is the widest column at 220px, wider than Feature and Free together, so a secondary annotation dominates the hierarchy. The table overflows by 257px, Enterprise is clipped at the box edge, and the reader must scroll far right to reach Notes.
critique.cause: Notes at 220px (199px text) over-allocates space to prose, while Enterprise at 105px (84px text) still wraps Support to three lines. The 104/100/87 plan minima plus the 220px Notes column push the total to 617px.

critique.good: Closest to the 360px box at 461px, with only 101px overflow. Free, Pro and Enterprise are near their no-split minima, and no words split mid-word.
critique.problems: Rows are 153–176px tall with large empty areas under short values, making the table 707px tall and hard to scan. Notes is still off-screen despite the overflow, and Feature wraps 'SSO / SAML' and 'Audit log', adding height.
critique.cause: Notes is only 96px (75px text) for 419px of prose, forcing six to seven lines and driving every row height. Feature at 78px (57px text) is tight enough to wrap row labels. The design pays 101px of overflow without giving Notes enough width to reduce height.

critique.good: Free and Pro are near ideal widths, all headers and short plan values stay intact, and the long Enterprise support value wraps cleanly at word boundaries with no mid-word splits.
critique.problems: Notes is entirely outside the 360px box; rows are 106–129px tall because the hidden Notes column is only 133px wide; Feature at 80px forces SSO / SAML and Audit log onto two lines; Enterprise at 108px is still cut by the box.
critique.cause: Widths sum to 508px. Notes 133px leaves only 112px of text for 419px of prose, so its five-line cells set row height. The first four columns total 375px, so the plan set cannot fit visibly; Feature is 24px below the 104px needed for SSO / SAML on one line.

critique.good: It has the smallest overflow of the three current designs at 121px, Free and Pro remain readable, the Enterprise header survives, and there are no mid-word splits.
critique.problems: It is the tallest table at 614px; Notes is only a clipped sliver at the right; its 119px width creates five- and six-line cells and 129–153px rows; Enterprise at 96px makes the long support value four lines; Feature at 78px wraps SSO / SAML and Audit log.
critique.cause: Total 480px still overflows, but the allocation starves Notes to save width. Notes prose needs 419px on one line, so at 98px of text it wraps to six lines and drives every row height, trading horizontal overflow for vertical bloat.

critique.good: Shortest table at 498px; Feature at 96px and Enterprise at 108px make the plan columns comfortable; headers and short values are intact; Notes at 140px reduces some rows to four lines.
critique.problems: Widest overflow at 172px; at 360px the Enterprise header and values are cut by the dashed box; Notes is still offscreen; Feature at 96px still wraps SSO / SAML, so that extra width buys little; total width is 532px.
critique.cause: The design over-invests in Feature and Enterprise while leaving Notes at 140px. Feature needs 104px for SSO / SAML on one line, so 96px still wraps it; Enterprise 108px helps the long value but does not justify the 172px overflow, and Notes still wraps to four lines.

understanding.purpose: A feature-by-feature plan comparison: readers check what each tier includes and use Notes for caveats.
understanding.reading: Scan down the Feature column, then move horizontally across Free, Pro and Enterprise to compare the same capability; Notes is consulted only when a value needs explanation.
groups: Free, Pro and Enterprise are parallel plan-value columns and should read as a comparable set
Feature is the row-label column that anchors each comparison
Notes is a secondary annotation column, not a fourth plan
keep_intact: the headers Feature, Free, Pro, Enterprise, Notes
short values such as 3, 2 GB, 100 GB, 30 days, 1 year, Custom and Email
Community and Unlimited where the chosen width permits
SSO / SAML as a single label
may_wrap: SSO / SAML at the slash if the Feature column is tight
long plan values at word boundaries when space is squeezed

bad.why: Squeezes every column, including Notes down to 75px of text, so the free-text column collapses into 7-line fragments and the table balloons to 707px tall; rows 153–176px high destroy the vertical rhythm that makes a comparison table scannable, and 'Feature'/'Audit log' also wrap.

Same failure in the extreme: Notes at 73px of text (7 lines, 730px table), plus a 1px-under-budget total that gains nothing — the narrowest table of the set is also the tallest, so the squeeze buys no legibility anywhere.

Worst of both worlds: the four plan columns still exceed the box (Enterprise clipped mid-header at 87px of text) while Notes at 112px of text still runs to 5 lines and 106–129px rows — it neither keeps the comparison in view nor makes the notes readable.

Notes at 98px of text gives 6-line cells and 129–153px rows, and Enterprise is again cut off at the box edge; the table is 614px tall and still scrolls 121px, paying both costs without collecting either benefit.

final.rationale: Every candidate overflows 360px, so the real decision is where the cut falls: r3B places the four comparison columns (77+100+87+96 = 360) exactly inside the box, so the reader can compare plans without scrolling and only the supplementary Notes column is pushed off-screen. Because Notes then gets 139px of text, rows stay at 83–106px and the whole table is 474px tall — the compact version of the same content. The Feature column at 77px breaks 'SSO / SAML' at its slash rather than mid-word, costing one extra line in one row, which is a fair trade for keeping Enterprise fully visible. Designs that clip Enterprise mid-header (r1B, r2A, r2B, r2C) break the very comparison the table exists for; designs that starve Notes (r1C, r3C) turn prose into seven-line fragments.

general: In a horizontally scrolling table, spend the scroll on the free-text/notes column, not on the columns the reader must compare side by side — a clipped comparison column breaks the table's core task, a clipped notes column merely defers it.

Give a prose column enough width to break at clause boundaries; below roughly 15–20 characters per line every cell becomes a fragment stack and row height explodes, which is worse than horizontal scrolling.

Columns playing the same role (Free/Pro/Enterprise) should be near-equal and sized to their longest token; the row-label and notes columns are different roles and deserve visibly different widths. Symmetry here would be a fault.
A row-label column may be narrower than its widest phrase if the break falls on a natural separator (space, slash) — a one-line cost in one row is cheaper than 20px stolen from every other column.
specific: The four plan columns need 387px at their natural one-line minimum (83+79+66+75 plus 84px padding), just over the 360px box, so some clipping or squeezing is unavoidable; the only free variable is how much overflow to accept and where.
The Notes column's one-line width is 419px, so it can never be one-line at any viable total — it is structurally the designated scroll target and should be sized for readability, not for fitting.
'Enterprise' at exactly 75px of available text in r3B has zero slack; a different font stack or subpixel rounding could wrap it, which argues for a few px of headroom if the budget allows.

final.tradeoffs: r1B is the honest rival: its rows are the shortest (358px table, 3-line maximum) and its Notes column at 199px reads as real sentences, which is the best notes legibility of the set — but it pays with 257px of scroll and clips 'Enterprise' mid-word, so the comparison only works after scrolling. A designer who treats Notes as primary content and the plans as a header row could legitimately choose it; one who treats the plan comparison as the table's job must choose r3B or r2C.
final.uncertain: Whether the 1px overshoot (360 vs the 359 budget) in r3B/r3A is acceptable, and whether the Notes column should exist at all at this width — dropping it, or moving it to a second line spanning under each row, may be a better answer than any width assignment. I am also not certain how much the exact 75px fit of 'Enterprise' depends on rendering.

A.why: Squeezes all five columns into 360px, splitting headers and values into fragments such as 'Featur e', 'Enterp rise', 'Unlimit ed', 'Custo m' and 'Comm unity'; the table fits but is hard to scan and compare.

B.why: The four plan columns stay intact and readable, with Free/Pro/Enterprise in a sensible progression; Notes is pushed off-screen, but the visible primary comparison works well.

C.why: Best balance of the visible columns: Feature, Free and Pro are intact, Enterprise gets enough width for its longer values, and the plan columns fit the 360px frame; Notes remains off-screen but scrollable.

D.why: Primary columns are readable and unsplit, but Enterprise is over-wide and the first four columns already slightly exceed the available width, adding unnecessary horizontal scroll while Notes remains off-screen.

E.why: Similar to D with a wider Feature and narrower Enterprise; readable, but still slightly overflows and gives no clear advantage over C.

F.why: Enterprise is excessively wide, creating large empty areas and forcing a larger horizontal scroll while Notes disappears completely; the three-line support value does not justify the lost width.

reviewsOld.unsure: The full width and readability of the off-screen Notes column cannot be verified from the screenshots; row heights suggest it remains narrow in every layout, which affects the overall judgment.
